messages:
anya: heads-up — CI evals for the quantized bring-up (q4_0) are showing nondeterministic outputs. ran the same commit twice on the nightly job and got different rouge/metric values. repro steps below.

anya: command i used:
```
./eval-runner --model=redwood/q4_0:rev-12 --dataset=webbench-1k --seed=42 --top_p=0.9 --temperature=0.0 --batch_size=1 --workers=4 --quant=true
```

anya: run A summary: ROUGE-L=0.412, exact_match=0.78
anya: run B summary (same commit + config): ROUGE-L=0.398, exact_match=0.74

matt: rough checklist — tokenizer pinned? rounding-mode env var? CI machine image identical? :thinking:

anya: tokenizer==v2.1.0 pinned in lockfile. image sha same. also repeated locally on a dev box under the same conda env and saw divergence.

kai: can you paste the raw outputs for a failing example (the text tokens)? might be subtle tokenization or sampling ordering.

anya: logs for prompt id=8932:
```
-- run A --
PROMPT: "Summarize the policy in one line"
OUT: "Policy is to route inference through the dedicated runtime for regulated workloads."
-- run B --
OUT: "Policy is to route inference via the dedicated runtime for regulated workloads."
```
anya: small change in preposition changed metric by a bunch on a short prompt.

lenka: hmm could be KV-cache not fully cleared between replications in the worker pool. we had a bug like that where a reused worker kept tail state.

sanjay: also recall we hit nondet in one of the int8 matmul kernels on Ampere when using XLA-like optimizations — quant kernel produced slightly different rounding depending on thread scheduling. worth checking kernel version.

matt: try `--workers=1 --batch_size=1 --disable-worker-reuse` and re-run twice to see if worker-pool reuse is the culprit.

anya: did that — workers=1 + disable-worker-reuse reduces frequency but i still got a mismatch once in 20 runs. so probably multiple contributors (sampling pipeline + quant kernel nondet).

kai: can you enable RNG state dumps in the runner? e.g. `RNG_DUMP=/tmp/rng-<id>.json` so we can diff PRNG state between runs. also ensure all RNG sources are seeded: python, numpy, torch, internal samplers.

lenka: add to that: snapshot the model binary checksum and quant kernel commit id. put both into the job metadata so CI artifacts have reproducible trace.

anya: putting a tiny trace here — sample RNG states looked identical, but the op trace shows a different thread id executing the quant matmul on run B.

eva-bot: CI job 3429 finished — artifacts: build/q4_0/rev-12.tar.gz, logs/1976543210/{runA.log,runB.log}, rng-dumps/{8932-runA.json,8932-runB.json}

anya: filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/issues/125 — minimal reproducer + artifacts attached. cc @kai @sanjay

kai: i'll pick this up tomorrow, first step: reproduce with a minimal C++ kernel-only harness (no tokenizer, no batching) to isolate numeric nondet. if we reproduce, we'll bisect kernel commits.

lenka: also adding a CI guard: repeat-same-seed 2x and fail if outputs differ more than tiny threshold; put behind a flag for nightly runs to avoid blocking devs.

sanjay: logging improvement: persist a tiny op-execution trace + thread id + affinity at time of matmul for failing runs. will help correlate with kernel scheduler.

anya: awesome, thanks. i've added the CI wing and linked the nightly job. will follow up after kai's kernel-level repro. staying out of the exec hot-path for now. :thumbsup:
